I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` skill because this is a contract review of code shipped with the CLI. I’ll validate the supplied scan against the fixture source, then rank concrete production failures separately from maintainability-only drift.

The skill file isn’t present under the runner subdirectory, so I’m resolving it from the repository path listed in the session instructions and continuing without changing files.

The scan is reproducible: 5 findings. Source inspection reveals the route detector understates the runtime contract breakage because two URLs are assembled dynamically or use a literal `:id`; I’m including those concrete failures rather than treating the detector list as exhaustive.

The client/API contract is broken in five areas. The most dangerous failure is a request that succeeds while returning the wrong tenant data.

## Ranked production impact

1. **Critical — seat lookup silently targets the wrong tenant and returns fabricated data.**  
   The client sends the literal path `/api/teams/:id/seats`; it never interpolates `id` ([workspace-client.ts](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:27>)). FastAPI accepts `:id` as the `team_id`, so this can return HTTP 200 rather than exposing the mistake. The backend then ignores `team_id` and always calculates seats for `Plan.FREE` ([routes.py](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:20>)). Every workspace therefore appears to have one seat.

2. **High — changing a plan cannot work; three contract mismatches are stacked.**  
   At [workspace-client.ts:33](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:33>), the client:

   - uses `PUT`, while the API declares `POST` ([routes.py:25](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:25>)); current result: **405**;
   - sends the literal `:id`, so the requested workspace ID is discarded;
   - never sends `plan`. FastAPI treats the scalar `plan: str` parameter as a required query parameter, so correcting only the method would produce **422**.

3. **High — workspace creation always hits a nonexistent route.**  
   The client calls `POST /api/workspaces` ([workspace-client.ts:22](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:22>)); the API exposes `POST /api/teams` ([routes.py:15](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:15>)). Current result: **404**. After fixing the path, the client would still receive **422**, because the API requires a dictionary body and the client sends none.

4. **High — workspace retrieval always hits a nonexistent route.**  
   `getWorkspace` calls `/api/workspaces/{id}` ([workspace-client.ts:17](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:17>)), while the backend exposes `/api/teams/{team_id}` ([routes.py:10](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:10>)). Current result: **404**. `crimes` missed this instance because the URL is assembled dynamically.

5. **Medium — the closed set of plans has diverged.**  
   Python defines `free | pro | team | scale` ([plans.py:10](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10>)); TypeScript defines `free | pro | enterprise` ([workspace-client.ts:10](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10>)).

   - `team` and `scale` are not modeled by the UI.
   - `enterprise` does not exist in the backend’s canonical enum.
   - TypeScript types disappear at runtime, while the mutation endpoint accepts unvalidated `str`, so invalid plans may pass through instead of failing cleanly.

6. **Low — the same tenant concept is named differently.**  
   The client consistently says “workspace”; the API says “team.” This does not independently break requests, but it caused the route drift above and makes future cross-stack changes easy to miss.

The scan’s `name_behavior_mismatch` finding for `getWorkspace` is not a client/API disagreement and is likely noise: fetching is normal behavior for an asynchronous getter. Suggested feedback:

```bash
crimes feedback 'name_behavior_mismatch::packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts::getWorkspace' --verdict fp --note "An async API getter is expected to perform an HTTP fetch; the name does not imply local purity."
```

The JSON/TOML coverage warnings do not hide additional contracts here; those files contain only scanner configuration and package metadata. No tests are present to catch any of these failures.
